A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Minnow research work. All 29 pages of v1 and 34 pages of v2, including appendices A–H and A–I respectively, provide readable text, equations, figures, and tables supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original training and evaluation results for held-out word classification, syntactic classification, usage generation, and definition generation, with additional results and analyses in the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experiments and adds Llama-2/CoLLEGe comparisons and original BLiMP evaluation results in Appendix I.

M1.justification: The episodic masked-word training, shared placeholder and separator tokens, next-token objective, language-modeling mixture, and embedding-only LLM finetuning remain unchanged. The Llama-2 experiments apply the existing Minnow procedure to another backbone.

E1.justification: v2 adds BLiMP as a supplementary evaluation of general grammatical competence rather than newly learned words (Appendix I). The original training corpora and word-learning datasets and tasks are retained, making this a focused extension of coverage.

E2.justification: v1 included CoLLEGe only through externally reported definition-generation scores with comparability caveats. v2 directly evaluates CoLLEGe in classification and generation comparisons and adds off-the-shelf Llama-2 7B controls alongside Minnow on that backbone. This substantially strengthens comparator coverage across the experiments.

E3.justification: v2 adds matched Llama-2 7B configurations and comparator-specific evaluation procedures. The syntactic baseline expands from 'dax' to 'dax', 'wug', and 'blicket' (Figure 2). CoLLEGe definition generation omits usage examples from the decoder prompt, unlike v1's imported 'Prompting + CoLLEGe' setup; these are different experimental conditions.

E4.justification: Appendix I introduces a dedicated analysis of whether Minnow finetuning harms existing grammatical capabilities. New Tables 13 and 15 and the expanded Oxford examples in Table 19 add comparative CoLLEGe failure and case analyses. Existing Llama-3 analyses remain, while the 'swiz' case in Table 4 is removed.

E5.justification: v2 adds standard deviations and plotted confidence intervals for the Llama-3 syntactic baseline alongside its broader placeholder settings (Table 7 and Figure 2); v1 reported fixed-'dax' point estimates. Minnow's existing three-run, seed, and uncertainty-reporting practices are retained.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive Llama-2/CoLLEGe results, including 74% versus 13% greedy usage-generation wins on BabyLM-10M (Table 1), and replaces imported CoLLEGe definition scores under a different setup. The syntactic baseline changes from approximately 64% to 66% alongside revised placeholder conditions. New BLiMP results show 83.5% baseline versus 83.3% Minnow overall, with a 9.7-point decrease on one NPI subset (Table 20).

T1.justification: The episodic objective and conditional-likelihood classification mathematics are retained. Appendix C adds worked examples explaining the existing classifier, without introducing new definitions, derivations, assumptions, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract and central introduction/conclusion claims remain: Minnow enables data-efficient few-shot word learning from scratch and improves pretrained LLM word classification and generation. The added comparisons support these retained contributions without redefining them.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly equates word and concept learning, adds specific limitations of automatic metrics and LLM judges, and elaborates continual-learning proposals. Appendix I introduces an interpretation of largely preserved capabilities while acknowledging an outlier. Much of the morphological caution already appeared in v1 Appendix H.

D1.justification: v2 adds CoLLEGe checkpoint, embedding-use, and generation-prompt details. Appendix A newly clarifies that the CHILDES snapshot differs from the cited preprocessing study and the currently available corpus; this documents provenance rather than establishing a dataset change. Existing hyperparameters, hardware information, and the code-release promise remain.

R1.justification: v2 adds references concerning concept learning, morphological families, evaluator reliability, RoBERTa, and BLiMP, and develops the comparison with CoLLEGe. The main related-work organization and the positioning of Minnow against embedding-based word learning remain substantially intact.

P1.justification: v2 adds a CoLLEGe baseline subsection, a worked classification example in Appendix C, expanded limitations, and Appendix I. Local wording and captions are revised, but the abstract, main narrative, method exposition, and overall section sequence remain largely stable.

P2.justification: Comparative displays expand substantially: Figure 2 grows from four to seven model series; Tables 1, 3, and 6 gain model entries; and new syntactic, case-analysis, and BLiMP tables appear. The Oxford definition table gains a CoLLEGe column, while Table 4 loses one example. Other appendix tables are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses an important weakness in v1: its closest meta-learning comparator appeared only through explicitly non-comparable literature scores. Direct CoLLEGe evaluations with Llama-2 backbone controls across classification and generation substantially improve the comparative evidence. Baseline uncertainty, grammar-retention testing, and specific evaluation caveats further strengthen assessment. Changed CoLLEGe prompting and the conflicting source note in Table 17 still limit part of the comparison, but do not outweigh these gains.
